extract:
Extract evidence for dietary salt/sodium intake and incident hypertension from the supplied original title and abstract. Return the schema JSON in concise English.
PICOS: P is the population in the hypertension-incidence analysis, excluding calibration samples. Include the longitudinal sample size when reported. Write only study facts: do not repeat extraction instructions or discuss calibration when no calibration sample is mentioned. I and C are the salt/sodium exposure and its actual reference group. Preserve the original direction: higher versus lower intake in cohorts, sodium reduction versus usual intake in trials. Retain questionnaire-based salty-food frequency categories as stated. Use each paper's actual reference category, which need not be the absolute lowest. O is Incident hypertension. S is design and follow-up. Do not add full-text details or invented intake cutoffs. Do not transfer intake means or participant counts from mortality/CVD analyses to a different hypertension-incidence subcohort. When a category/reference is not specified, say that concisely. Each PICOS text <=115 characters. Preserve intake assessment and timing (baseline, mean or most recent) when reported.
Effects: retain numerical findings for the highest versus lowest reported intake groups, otherwise the explicitly stated higher-versus-lower reference, or isolated sodium reduction versus usual care. Preserve separate methods, models and within-subgroup comparisons. Exclude intermediate intake levels when the extreme contrast is reported: for second-through-fifth versus first groups, return only fifth versus first. Exclude comparisons that jointly change sodium and genotype, baseline BP or potassium. A sodium comparison WITHIN a genotype or other subgroup is eligible. Exclude other nutrients, weight loss, combined weight-loss-plus-sodium interventions, serum sodium/osmolarity effects, salt sensitivity, BP changes, prevalence and cardiovascular outcomes.
Prefer the directly reported comparative effect (HR, OR, RR, risk difference, or relative percent reduction) over descriptive arm rates. If the article has any eligible comparative effect, return only comparative effects and no cumulative-incidence rows from that article. Use the paper's metric, with HR/OR/RR/RD abbreviations; preserve other names even if a different metric is conventional for its model. Keep reported percent reductions as percentages; do not convert them to ratios. If a ratio and its percent reduction describe the same comparison, keep only the ratio; use a percent-reduction row only when no ratio is reported. Do not calculate or invert an estimate. If only cumulative incidences for both exposure and comparator groups are reported, record ONE row per comparison: effect_type = Cumulative incidence, effect_value = exposure-group percentage, comparator_estimate = comparator-group percentage, unit = %. For every other measure comparator_estimate must be null. When every category including the lowest has an HR with a nondegenerate CI, do not assume the lowest category is the HR reference; retain explicitly reported extreme-group cumulative incidences instead. Never assign an RR range summarizing several distinct intervention arms to sodium alone. With no eligible quantitative result, return effects: [].
Keep intervention and comparator <=95 characters and adjustment <=140 characters. Dimensionless ratios and risk differences have unit=null. Preserve null/nonsignificant results. Methods-section adjustment applies when linked to the reported effect, including inverse-probability weighting for adjusted survival/risk differences. If an unadjusted number is reported and the adjusted association became nonsignificant, record both facts in adjustment. CI fields hold only the stated 95% confidence limits for the exact comparative estimate; group rates must have null CI fields unless an unambiguous interval for the exposure group is reported. Preserve timepoint and P-value meaning, including trend or interaction labels. Do not treat a global log-rank P value as a pairwise comparison P value.
Every source_quote must be an exact contiguous substring of the supplied title or abstract. Numeric result quotes include the number and its context; multi-estimate sentences retain enough text to identify the correct groups. Preserve spelling and case. Use no other sources.

The schema above defines the required fields; do not reproduce the schema. Return a populated extraction object with top-level keys picos and effects, using the article supplied in the user message.
NC evidence fields: S starts with the study-design category RCT, OS, MR, META, SR, REVIEW or Others, followed by the specific design and follow-up. Classify EACH reported effect using only its own comparison, subgroup, timepoint and adjustment model.
exposure_direction: increased for higher salt/sodium versus lower; decreased for sodium reduction versus usual care; not found when unspecified.
effect_direction: direction of the reported outcome point estimate for intervention/exposure versus comparator: increase, decrease, no_change, or not found. For ratios compare with 1; for differences compare with 0; for paired incidences compare exposure with comparator; a reported percentage reduction means decrease. Keep this point-estimate direction even if nonsignificant.
significance: positive for statistical significance, negative for nonsignificance, not found when not established for this exact comparison. A stated 95% CI excluding its null implies positive; including the null implies negative (ratio null=1, difference null=0). Use this exact estimate's CI before a different model's statement. With no CI, use an explicitly linked pairwise P value or a direct statement for this comparison. Trend, interaction and global P values cannot determine pairwise significance. A descriptive difference between group percentages alone cannot determine significance. Do not transfer significance between models, methods or subgroups. significance_basis is 95% CI, P value, Reported statement, or Not found. significance_quote is an exact contiguous abstract passage supporting this classification, or empty when not found.
effect_type is the reported statistical metric: HR for hazard ratio, OR for odds ratio, RR for relative risk/risk ratio, RD for risk difference. Use a concise reported name for other metrics, such as Cumulative incidence, Relative reduction or Multivariate risk. effect_value is the numerical value. Keep the original reported value without inversion or conversion.

map:
Identify the biomedical and study-design entities represented in the extracted PICOS and effect estimates. Use the original abstract to ground every entity. Include only entities represented in the focused extracted fields, not every topic mentioned elsewhere in the abstract. The focused outcome is incident hypertension; omit other outcomes such as blood-pressure change when absent from the extracted fields. Return JSON {"entities":[{"concept_id":string or null,"label":string,"mention":string,"role":"P"|"I"|"C"|"O"|"S","source_quote":string}]}.
Choose concept_id from the supplied terminology index when the concept matches. An index entry represents its named concept; the vocabulary mappings can be broader and do not change that concept's meaning. Use null and a concise English label for an entity absent from the index. Do not invent codes. Include each distinct population condition/demographic, intervention component, comparator component, outcome and design. Do not add entities mentioned only as background or negated conditions. Do not infer a disease diagnosis from a blood-pressure measurement, or an age category from a mean age. Preserve resistant/uncontrolled hypertension, sodium or potassium intake, urinary measurement, excretion, and ratios as distinct concepts. Include systolic/diastolic/mean arterial pressure separately where stated. Expand abbreviations using the abstract. "Salt Control H" is salt-monitoring equipment: choose salt_monitoring_device, never salt_substitute. "SaltSwitch" is a mobile application. "NOx" denotes nitric oxide metabolites; choose nitric_oxide_metabolites. Include named intervention devices/brands as entities; use null rather than omit them when no index concept matches. Exclude statistical tests, place names, sample sizes, numbers, doses, durations and generic "control group", "usual care", "usual diet", "recommended diet" or named cohort participants; these remain in the evidence table. Do not list generic parent concepts when a more specific index entity already captures the mention in the same role.
Assign roles from the extracted fields: P contains participant demographics, eligibility and baseline conditions; I and C contain the exposure or intervention and its reference group; O contains measured outcomes; S contains the design of this study. For these incident-hypertension studies, normotensive, nonhypertensive, and free-of-hypertension eligibility describe the absence of baseline disease. Never map those population phrases to the hypertension concept or a hypertension disease code; hypertension belongs to the outcome role. A dietary exposure mentioned in the background does not describe the study population. Ground source_quote in the study's methods or results; exclude claims about prior literature and research gaps. For a structured abstract, do not use the Background section as evidence for a study entity. Prefer the comparison sentence for exposure and comparator entities, retaining higher/lower qualifiers in the original mention when available.
One row per distinct concept and PICOS role, at most 30 rows. mention and source_quote must each be exact contiguous nonempty substrings of the original title or abstract; the quote must contain the mention. Preserve the original case. Prefer a short sentence or clause for source_quote. label is the full English concept name. For intervention-related changes reported as outcomes, use role O. Return only the JSON object.
